requirements.fact: The law and safety standards require a separate observer to watch the skier continuously.
requirements.misconception: A boat operator can easily watch the skier behind the boat while steering forward.
pamphlet_excerpts: Engine Shutdown Protocol: Turn off the boat motor completely before any skier approaches the boarding ladder.
Submerged Debris Survey: Scout shallow water zones and sandbars prior to towing skiers at high speeds.
Tow Line Clearance: Keep floating towlines away from rotating boat propellers to prevent sudden line entanglements.
Weather Awareness Standards: Cease all towing operations immediately whenever lightning strikes or dense fog develops offshore.
requirements.pamphlet_summary: Towed water sports introduce acute environmental hazards including propeller strikes, submerged obstacles, and collision with other watercraft. Skiers and boat crews maintain continuous vigilance by surveying ski courses and monitoring changing marine weather conditions.
requirements.safety_callout: Always shut down the boat engine before bringing a fallen skier alongside or onto the swim platform.
socratic_questions: Why must a boat driver never turn backward to observe a fallen skier?
How do unseen floating deadheads create catastrophic dangers for towed water skiers?
What specific environmental changes signal an immediate return to the boat dock?
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Course Reconnaissance: Survey the planned tow corridor for shallow sandbars, floating logs, and mooring buoys.
Step 2 - Crew Assignment: Station a dedicated driver and an alert safety observer inside the towboat.
Step 3 - Equipment Check: Examine the tow rope and bridle hardware for strand fraying and knots.
Step 4 - Emergency Drill: Practice rapid engine cutoffs and recovery approaches during a simulated skier fall.

sub_requirements.fact: Hitting water at thirty miles per hour causes severe contusions and concussion trauma.
sub_requirements.misconception: Water provides a completely soft surface that prevents physical impact injuries during falls.
sub_requirements.pamphlet_summary: Skiing zones present significant dangers like shallow water, docks, swimmer zones, and high-speed wake turbulence. Ski crews mitigate risk through thorough course mapping and establishing wide safety margins from shorelines.

sub_requirements.fact: Immersion in water below sixty degrees Fahrenheit triggers involuntary gasping and rapid hypothermia.
sub_requirements.misconception: Cold water shock only occurs in freezing winter lakes during ice-out conditions.
sub_requirements.pamphlet_summary: Continuous handle friction produces palm blisters while prolonged water exposure induces hypothermia and muscle cramps. Early recognition of shivering, confusion, or skin breakdown allows immediate onshore first aid.

sub_requirements.fact: Safety Afloat governs all Scouting motorized watercraft activities including skiing and wakeboarding.
sub_requirements.misconception: Safety Afloat guidelines apply only to human-powered canoes, kayaks, and rowboats.
sub_requirements.pamphlet_summary: Safety Afloat mandates qualified supervision, physical fitness, swimming defense, life jackets, and designated rescue equipment. Every water sports activity requires strict adherence to these nine operational points.

requirements.fact: High-speed water impacts can prevent automatic inflation or tear lightweight inflatable chambers instantly.
requirements.misconception: Inflatable life vests work well for water skiing because they are lightweight and unobtrusive.
pamphlet_excerpts: Impact Rating Mandate: Select life jackets constructed with heavy-duty foam designed to withstand high-velocity water impacts.
Buckle Tension Standard: Fasten every buckle and cinch straps snugly to prevent slippage over the head.
Code Compliance Rule: Never ski after sunset or before sunrise regardless of clear ambient weather conditions.
Carbon Monoxide Defense: Avoid teak surfing or dragging behind boat exhaust outlets to prevent poisonings.
requirements.pamphlet_summary: Towed water sports require rugged, Coast Guard approved life jackets equipped with secure multi-buckle closures. Skiers commit to the Water Sports Safety Code to preserve discipline, communication, and mutual safety across the crew.
requirements.safety_callout: Never use an ill-fitting or non-impact-rated life jacket during water sports activities.
socratic_questions: Why will an unconscious skier drown without a properly secured, inherently buoyant life jacket?
What structural differences distinguish a water-ski vest from a standard paddle-craft life jacket?
Which element of the Water Sports Safety Code prevents severe propeller lacerations?
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Label Verification: Inspect the inner Coast Guard approval stamp for correct weight and chest sizing.
Step 2 - Vest Fitting: Put on the vest and snap each chest buckle from bottom to top.
Step 3 - Shoulder Pull: Pull upward firmly on shoulder straps to verify the vest stays below chin.
Step 4 - Code Review: Rehearse all rules in the safety code aloud with the boat driver.

sub_requirements.fact: Loose life jackets can ride up over the face and obstruct breathing during falls.
sub_requirements.misconception: A loose life jacket is safer because it allows freer arm movement while turning.
sub_requirements.pamphlet_summary: Water ski vests feature impact-resistant nylon shells, durable closed-cell foam, and three or four webbed buckle straps. A proper snug fit ensures the jacket stays securely on the body during violent crashes.

sub_requirements.fact: The safety code constitutes strict operating rules mandated by maritime law and Scouting policy.
sub_requirements.misconception: The safety code is merely optional advice that boaters can discard on quiet lakes.
sub_requirements.pamphlet_summary: The Water Sports Safety Code establishes rules against night skiing, riding boat gunwales, and skiing in shallow areas. Committing to this code protects both participants and non-participating boaters sharing open public waterways.

requirements.fact: Every participant must pass the standard swimmer test before beginning water sports instruction.
requirements.misconception: Wearing a life jacket allows a non-swimmer to bypass the required swimmer test.
pamphlet_excerpts: Distance Swimming Benchmark: Swim seventy-five yards using a strong, well-executed forward crawl or trudgen stroke.
Resting Stroke Transition: Complete the final twenty-five yards using an easy, restful elementary backstroke.
Water Entry Standard: Leap feetfirst into water over your head before beginning the continuous stroke trial.
Floating Endurance Demonstration: Rest by floating motionless on your back for one minute following the swim.
requirements.pamphlet_summary: The swimmer test establishes foundational aquatic competency required before attempting deepwater starts or towed maneuvers. Candidates complete one hundred yards using strong forward strokes followed by an unassisted resting float.
requirements.safety_callout: Conduct all swimmer classification tests in calm water under certified lifeguard supervision.
socratic_questions: Why must a skier demonstrate independent swimming proficiency even while wearing a life jacket?
How does the floating requirement demonstrate self-rescue ability in open deep water?
What physiological advantages does a restful backstroke provide during an unexpected open-water separation?
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Feetfirst Entry: Jump feetfirst into water over your head and level off into swimming position.
Step 2 - Forward Propulsion: Swim seventy-five yards using a continuous, propulsive crawl or breaststroke without stopping.
Step 3 - Stroke Transition: Roll over smoothly to swim twenty-five yards using an elementary backstroke technique.
Step 4 - Motionless Float: Float motionless on your back for one full minute to demonstrate resting stamina.

requirements.fact: Outboard engine roar and wind noise completely drown out shouts from a towed skier.
requirements.misconception: Yelling loudly from behind the boat is an effective way to request speed changes.
pamphlet_excerpts: Speed Increase Gesture: Extend one hand forward with thumb pointed distinctly upward toward the tow boat.
Speed Reduction Signal: Point the thumb downward toward the water to instruct the driver to decelerate.
Motor Cutoff Command: Draw a flat hand firmly across the throat to demand immediate engine shutdown.
Skier Safe Posture: Clasp both hands together overhead to signal no injury occurred after a fall.
requirements.pamphlet_summary: Engine noise prevents verbal communication across the tow rope, making standardized hand signals essential for skier safety. The skier communicates speed adjustments, directional changes, emergency stops, and physical status clearly to the observer.
requirements.safety_callout: Signal skier safe immediately after falling so the observer knows you are conscious and uninjured.
socratic_questions: Why must the safety observer watch the skier rather than the boat operator doing so?
Why is holding a ski vertically out of the water important for a fallen skier?
Under what circumstances should a skier immediately give the cut motor hand signal?
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Signal Preparation: Establish eye contact with the boat safety observer before executing any hand signal.
Step 2 - Speed Modulation: Form clear thumbs-up or thumbs-down gestures to fine-tune the boat towing speed.
Step 3 - Directional Indication: Point with your open hand toward the left or right to command turns.
Step 4 - Recovery Signaling: Raise one ski or clasp hands overhead immediately upon falling into the water.

requirements.fact: Boat propulsion creates hydroplane lift, meaning the skier should remain crouched until planing occurs.
requirements.misconception: Standing up quickly by muscle force alone lifts the skier out of deep water.
pamphlet_excerpts: Deepwater Starting Posture: Keep knees bent deeply against chest while holding ski tips above the water.
Arms Straight Technique: Allow boat pull to draw body upward without prematurely pulling arms into chest.
Wake Crossing Angle: Attack wake crests at a sharp diagonal angle while keeping knees flexed.
Handle Release Procedure: Drop the tow handle cleanly and coast smoothly until momentum dissipates in water.
requirements.pamphlet_summary: Towed participants must display balance, proper body posture, and wave management across variable wake patterns. Mastery involves executing unassisted deepwater starts, carving across wake crests, and safely dismounting into open water.
requirements.safety_callout: Never wrap any part of the towline around hands, wrists, or limbs while skiing.
socratic_questions: Why does bending your knees help you maintain balance while crossing turbulent boat wakes?
How does leaning away from the boat facilitate aggressive carving across the wake crest?
What catastrophic injury can occur if a skier wraps the tow handle around their arm?
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Deepwater Setup: Crouch in deep water with ski tips protruding above surface between towline bridle.
Step 2 - Planing Phase: Let the boat pull you upright into a balanced athletic stance upon acceleration.
Step 3 - Wake Traversal: Lean outward and cut across both wakes diagonally with bent knees absorbing chop.
Step 4 - Controlled Dismount: Release the tow handle, sink into water hips-first, and protect your head.

sub_requirements.fact: Bending your arms exhausts back muscles and tips your center of balance backward.
sub_requirements.misconception: Pulling the handle inward toward your chest helps pull you out of the water.
sub_requirements.pamphlet_summary: Entering water safely involves slipping from the swim platform away from the propeller with equipment secured. The skier lets the engine draw them onto a plane while maintaining a tucked position with arms straight.

sub_requirements.fact: Hitting wakes parallel causes skis to slide sideways and triggers violent rotational falls.
sub_requirements.misconception: Skiing directly parallel across wake rollers prevents the ski tips from catching water.
sub_requirements.pamphlet_summary: Crossing wakes requires carving hard outside the rooster tail, leaning into turns, and cutting diagonally across the wake. The skier absorbs the double wake rollers with spring-loaded knees to avoid catching ski edges.

sub_requirements.fact: High-speed shore approaches risk catastrophic collisions with shallow bottoms, rocks, or shoreline docks.
sub_requirements.misconception: Skiing directly up to the beach at full speed makes for an impressive landing.
sub_requirements.pamphlet_summary: Skiers release the towline immediately to avoid imminent obstacles and slide safely into open water. When stopping, throwing the handle away and coasting prevents entanglement and avoids collisions with docks or shores.

requirements.fact: Water ski bindings must release the feet during violent falls to prevent severe lower-leg fractures.
requirements.misconception: Bindings should be tightened as rigidly as downhill snow ski boots to maximize control.
pamphlet_excerpts: Dry Binding Lubrication: Wet the rubber binding with lake water before sliding feet into the boots.
Heel Cup Alignment: Position your heel firmly against the rear cup before tightening overlay tension straps.
Deepwater Retrieval Drill: Swim toward floating skis using breaststroke while scanning continuously for approaching boat hulls.
In-Water Fitting Method: Submerge the ski tail beneath you to slide feet into bindings while floating.
requirements.pamphlet_summary: Properly adjusted rubber bindings hold feet snugly while permitting rapid release during high-speed water tumbles. Skiers must master wet adjustment methods and retrieve loose floating equipment independently in deep open water.
requirements.safety_callout: Never insert dry feet into rubber bindings because friction can tear delicate boot rubber or sprain ankles.
socratic_questions: Why must water ski bindings release your feet during a high-speed fall?
How do you maintain flotation and situational awareness while donning skis in deep water?
What dangers exist when swimming after a runaway ski in active motorboat traffic?
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Shoreline Sizing: Loosen binding laces, wet rubber boots, and slide feet in for snug fit.
Step 2 - Equipment Retrieval: Locate detached floating skis in deep water and gather them alongside your torso.
Step 3 - In-Water Mounting: Push the ski tail underwater while guiding your lubricated foot into front binding.
Step 4 - Rear Foot Insertion: Slip the rear foot into toe piece and cinch cords securely before signaling.
